title: Topological mass formula (Archimedean)
html:
Proposition. Topological mass formula (Archimedean)

Proposition. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be the \mathbb{C}-quantum observable universe and let K be a hyperbolic knot whose complement carries the vortex topology of a stable particle, generated by N blow-ups along the brane tower. Then the mass formula

  \mathfrak{m}(K) = \frac{\mathrm{Vol}(K)}{\hbar_q^{2}}

holds, where \mathrm{Vol}(K) is the hyperbolic volume of S^3 \setminus K and \hbar_q = 1 - 1/q is the quantum Planck constant (quantum Planck constant) at the substrate parameter q (substrate parameter). The descent involution \hat{\tau}_n (descent involution) induces the idempotent splitting \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A_{n+1}) = \mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{desc}} \oplus \mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{trans}} (descent eigenspaces); under the archimedean fibre functor, the descended trace evaluates to the holonomy \mathrm{Hol}_{\nabla_A} and each transient trace to the quantum dilogarithm \Phi_q(z_i).

The archimedean-realisation framing of this closed form is described in the topological mass-formula context.

Proof

The derivation proceeds from the categorical decomposition (topological mass) via three identifications, each following from the archimedean bridge.

Step 1 — baseline holonomy \mapsto hyperbolic volume. The descended trace of the universal vortex \varrho_0 is the holonomy norm \lVert \mathrm{Hol}_{\nabla_A}(\varrho_0; \mathfrak{G}) \rVert. Under the archimedean fibre functor (categorical-archimedean-bridge) this is the imaginary part of the Chern--Simons functional on the flat connection associated to K, which by the Chern–Simons / hyperbolic-volume correspondence equals \mathrm{Vol}(S^3 \setminus K) (Möbius energy; Kashaev volume density). Concretely,

  \mathrm{Re}\,\mathrm{tr}\bigl(\hat{\tau}_n^{\mathrm{desc}}\,\mathrm{Hol}\bigr)
  \;=\; \mathrm{Vol}(K).

Step 2 — transient dilogarithm sum \mapsto (1/\hbar_q^{2} - 1) correction. The transient eigenspace contributes one quantum-dilogarithm factor \Phi_q(z_i) per blow-up exceptional divisor. In the Briggs–Klein spectral coordinates of the brane tower (mass-endomorphism on the jet tower), the z_i are the eigenvalues of the per-crossing transfer operator on the curvature-rank stratification. Summing over the N blow-ups and using the dilogarithm identity \sum_{i=1}^N \Phi_q(z_i) = (1/\hbar_q^{2} - 1)\,\mathrm{Vol}(K) (Kashaev–Murakami volume conjecture restricted to the q-deformation; this is Hypothesis 2 (Dilogarithm evaluation) on the Lean structure qou:QOU.ArchimedeanMassFormula, field exceptional_sum_eq):

  \sum_{i=1}^{N} \Phi_q(z_i)
  \;=\; \mathrm{Vol}(K)\bigl(\hbar_q^{-2} - 1\bigr).

The Lean formalisation isolates this identity as a hypothesis on the archimedean structure rather than a derived theorem; the evaluation in Briggs–Klein coordinates is the categorical content the formula imports from the geometric side.

Step 3 — combine. Adding the baseline and transient contributions and recognising 1 + (\hbar_q^{-2} - 1) = \hbar_q^{-2}:

  \mathfrak{m}(K)
  \;=\; \mathrm{Vol}(K) + \mathrm{Vol}(K)\bigl(\hbar_q^{-2} - 1\bigr)
  \;=\; \frac{\mathrm{Vol}(K)}{\hbar_q^{2}}.

Combined with the knot--particle dictionary identifying particles with specific knots (e.g. the figure-eight knot 4_1 with the Higgs field), this formula determines the substrate parameter q from experimental mass ratios (see §6.10).
